Question
========
Consider the following XML document:

```
<location>
  <bike number="190301" state="ok"><battery_pack/></bike>
  <bike number="190302" state="ok"><battery_pack/></bike>
  <bike number="190303" state="error"><battery_pack/></bike>
</location>
```

What does the XPath expression `/location/bike[1]` select here?

Answerlist
----------
* Every `bike` element found anywhere inside the document.
* The first `bike` child of the `location` element - in this case, the bike with number `"190301"`.
* The `location` element itself.
* The last `bike` element inside the `location` element.


Solution
========
The path `/location/bike` selects `bike` elements that are direct children of `location`, and the index `[1]` narrows this down to just the first one in document order. In the document above, that is the bike with `number="190301"`.

Answerlist
----------
* False
* True
* False
* False
